note: Convention dictionary and repairs. (1) Incident flux: Tong's printed incident Poynting expression for a plane wave carries a c-factor inconsistency relative to E x B/mu0 elsewhere in the same notes (the historical scaffold note records 'repair T incident c factor'); Fitzpatrick's |<u>|=c eps0 E0^2/2 is dimensionally consistent. The framework uses only its own pthm-em-wave-energy-average result I=eps0 c |e|^2/2=|e|^2/(2 mu0 c) with mu0 eps0 c^2=1. (2) Beisert's dipole angular power c k^4 mu0 (...)/32 pi^2 and incident flux ||E0||^2/(2 eps0 c) are stated in his amplitude conventions; the framework rederives every constant in its own SI dictionary, where the angular power is mu0 omega^4 |n x p0|^2/(32 pi^2 c) and the incident flux |e|^2/(2 mu0 c). (3) Peatross and Ware's diffraction integral carries the Kirchhoff prefactor -i/lambda fixed by their appendix 10.A; the framework's model instead takes a finite complex aperture distribution (volts) with the outgoing Helmholtz kernel G_k and the absolute error terms of lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction, and records the overdetermined-trace caveat of lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation, so the two differ by that declared datum normalization only. (4) sinc is normalised identically (sin xi/xi for xi != 0, value 1 at 0). (5) Rayleigh, dielectric-sphere and inhomogeneity scattering are declined as material-response content; the astrophysical and circular-aperture applications are declined as out of the declared scope. (6) No measured values, precision or empirical claims are harvested from any of these treatments.
